- An expansion cadence (how many GPUs and when) tied to clear metrics so our CFO can model burn.
- Options for short-term surge/bursting without a long-term uplift in commitment.

Subject: RE: Dedicated cluster options & phased onramp — Amberfield pilot

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. I pulled together a concise matrix and proposed activation cadence (see inline below). Attached: amberfield-dedicated-options-20280620.pdf and an activation workbook that maps metrics to ramp triggers.

Quick summary (pilot → scale → steady-state):

1) Pilot (3 months, proof-of-concept)
- Cluster size: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (single AZ zone, dedicated pool)
- Minimum active GPUs: 4 (warm lanes) — allows headroom for autoscaling to 8
- Expected throughput: ~220 requests/sec for 512-token median requests (conservative)
- SLA targets: Latency p95 < 300ms (pilot SLO), uptime 99.5%
- Activation lead time: 7–10 business days
- Notes: includes prefix caching warmup for seeded workloads and 25% warmup credits to reduce cold-start noise.

2) Scale (month 4–9, expansion triggered by metrics)
- Trigger metric: sustained token consumption > 70% of pilot throughput over 14 days OR queueing events > 30s
- Cluster size options: 16 GPUs (preferred) → 32 GPUs (aggressive)
- Min active GPUs: floor = 8 for 16-GPU cluster; floor = 12 for 32-GPU cluster (maintain KV cache locality)
- Activation lead time: 10–14 business days (additional racks, cross-AZ if requested)
- Cost guidance: per-GPU committed rate plus incremental burst unit pricing for non-committed minutes.

3) Steady-state (month 9+, full commit)
- Typical committed footprints we recommend for production: 32–64 GPUs depending on multi-model fanout and peak concurrency
- Min active GPUs: 20% of committed pool (to preserve latency objectives)
- Operational callouts: canary rollouts, model pinning, automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants during overload.

Burst runway / surge options:
- Short-term burst: up to 2x peak for 48–72 hours via reserved burst credits (billed at premium).
- Graceful overflow: route traffic to burst lane in a different region or to a lower-cost quantized variant if latency budget allows.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa to confirm sizing assumptions (model family, sequence length distribution) and fill the activation worksheet.
- Ben to align commercial terms (commit bands and burst rates) with procurement.

I can convert this into the SOW exhibit language once we lock in the floor and burst bands.

Regards,
Jonas
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: amberfield-dedicated-options-20280620.pdf, activation-wave-worksheet.xlsx

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated cluster options & phased onramp — Amberfield pilot

Alex — quick technical note and a completed activation worksheet (see attached). I ran the amberfield sample traces you shared through our sizing model. Key assumptions I used (documented in the workbook):

- Model: 7B decoder-only family (fp16), median seq len 480, 95th seq len 1,024
- Concurrency profile: 80% short-chat, 20% long-form; peak concurrency factor 3.2x median
- Target p95 latency: 250ms for short-chat, up to 700ms acceptable for long-form during backfill windows

Updated sizing recommendations:
- Pilot: 6 committed GPUs, min active 3 — if you can tolerate p95 ≈ 320ms for pilot we can reduce cost. If you prefer tighter pilot SLO, stick with Jonas' 8 GPU pilot.
- Immediate scale gate (to 16 GPUs): when 95th percentile CPU/GPU utilization > 65% AND queue depth > 12 for 48h.
- Warmup strategy: staggered key-value cache priming across 3 waves (20% of tokens pre-populated per wave) to smooth memory pressure during activation.

Operational recommendations:
- Use a 2-week canary window on new model variants with traffic split 5%/95% before full cutover.
- Maintain a 10% buffer in the committed pool for maintenance and CUDA driver rollouts.

Attachments: activation-wave-worksheet.xlsx (filled), short-run-sla-comparison.csv (inline in worksheet).

Happy to hop on a short call to walk through the workbook and tune the triggers to your billing cadence.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
